LESSON: STRUCTURE OF THE ATOM

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.1: Structure of the atom

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Structure of the atom. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is the structure of the atom important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the structure of the atom
2. draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams
3. classify elements into metals and non- metals
4. show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STRUCTURE OF THE ATOM
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Structure of the atom helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: STRUCTURE OF THE ATOM
Study Structure of the atom like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the structure of the atom

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the structure of the atom. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the structure of the atom.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Structure of the atom” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the structure of the atom. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams

What this means
In this part you learn to draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Structure of the atom matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Classify elements into metals and non- metals

What this means
In this part you learn to classify elements into metals and non- metals. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify elements into metals and non- metals.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Structure of the atom this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify elements into metals and non- metals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals

What this means
In this part you learn to show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Structure of the atom” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Structure of the atom is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Structure of the atom” around your school. (skill: describe the structure of the atom)

Example 2: Say why Structure of the atom matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Structure of the atom this week. (skill: classify elements into metals and non- metals)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Structure of the atom” around your school. (skill: show interest in classifying elements into metals and non- metals)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Structure of the atom to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the structure of the atom.
3. Practise this skill: draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams.
4. Practise this skill: classify elements into metals and non- metals.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Structure of the atom from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Structure of the atom: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Structure of the atom?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is the structure of the atom important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Structure of the atom means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the structure of the atom.
5. Be able to: draw the electron arrangement in atoms using dot or cross diagrams.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
